questions.question: Which is the most common form of spam?
questions.explanation: Spam is any unwanted digital content, and email spam is its most common form.

questions.question: Which statement about binary (IEC) and decimal units is correct?

options.A: 1 KiB and a decimal KB both equal 1024 bytes
options.B: 1 KiB = 1000 bytes, while a decimal KB = 1024 bytes
options.C: 1 KiB = 1024 bits, while a decimal KB = 1000 bits
options.D: 1 KiB = 1024 bytes, while a decimal KB = 1000 bytes

questions.explanation: The kibibyte (KiB) is the binary unit of 1024 bytes; the decimal kilobyte is 10^3 = 1000 bytes.

questions.concept: LBA components absent from Moore machine definition
questions.question: Which components appear in the 8-tuple of a Linear Bounded Automaton but have no counterpart in the 6-tuple of a Moore machine?
questions.explanation: Both definitions contain Q, input alphabet, delta and q0; the end markers ML and MR (along with tape alphabet and final states) are LBA-specific.

questions.question: The word cryptography, derived from Greek roots, means:
questions.explanation: Cryptography derives from Greek roots meaning secret writing.

questions.question: C++ functions are broadly classified into which two types?

options.A: Standard library functions and user-defined functions

questions.explanation: C++ has standard library functions, which are predefined, and user-defined functions created by the programmer.

questions.question: What is the prefix form of the infix expression A + B * C ?
questions.explanation: B * C has higher precedence, becoming * B C, and the + is placed before both operands: + A * B C. A B C * + is the postfix form.

questions.concept: True division always returns a float
questions.question: What is the output of print(36 / 6)?
questions.explanation: The / operator performs true division and returns a float, so 36 / 6 gives 6.0. Floor division (//) would give 6.

questions.question: MICR, used for processing cheques, stands for:
questions.explanation: MICR stands for Magnetic Ink Character Recognition.

questions.question: HTTP was developed by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in which year?
questions.explanation: HTTP dates from 1989; 1990 is the WWW/HTML year, 1983 DNS and 1971 e-mail.

questions.question: Using FIFO page replacement with 3 frames (initially empty), how many page faults occur for the reference string 7, 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4, 2, 3?
questions.explanation: FIFO faults on 7, 0, 1, 2, 3, 0, 4, 2, 3 (hit only on the first repeated 0), giving 9 faults. LRU would give 8 and Optimal 6.

questions.concept: Simultaneous tuple assignment evaluates right side first
questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?
a, b = 5, 9
a, b = b, a + b
print(a, b)
questions.explanation: The right side is evaluated first using the old values, giving (9, 5 + 9) = (9, 14), and only then assigned to a and b.

questions.concept: Effect of rollback to savepoint before commit
questions.question: A transaction runs: INSERT row R1; SAVEPOINT s1; INSERT row R2; ROLLBACK TO s1; COMMIT;. Which rows are permanently saved?
questions.explanation: Rolling back to savepoint s1 undoes only the work after s1 (R2); COMMIT then makes R1 permanent.

questions.concept: Program in execution is a process
questions.question: In operating system terminology, what is a program in execution called?
questions.explanation: A program becomes a process when it is loaded and executing; it then moves through states such as new, ready, running and waiting.

questions.concept: Affiliate marketing as a three-party process
questions.question: Affiliate marketing is best described as a marketing process involving:

options.A: Four parties: bank, buyer, seller and government
options.B: Three parties: publisher, advertiser and consumer
options.C: Two parties: buyer and seller only
options.D: One party: the advertiser promoting itself

questions.explanation: Affiliate marketing is a three-party process where the publisher earns by referring consumers to the advertiser.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a Physical layer protocol?
questions.explanation: Physical layer protocols include DSL, ISDN, USB, Bluetooth and Ethernet; PPP is Data Link, ARP Network and MIME Presentation.

questions.concept: Reasoning about module design from cohesion and coupling
questions.question: Module X performs one well-defined function and exchanges data with only one other module. Module Y performs several unrelated jobs and depends on six other modules. Which statement is correct?

options.A: X has low cohesion and high coupling
options.B: X has high cohesion and low coupling
options.C: Y has low coupling but low cohesion
options.D: Y has high cohesion and low coupling

questions.explanation: Cohesion measures functional strength (X is focused, so high) and coupling measures interdependence (X has few dependencies, so low). Y is the opposite: low cohesion and high coupling.

questions.concept: Moore output fixed by present state
questions.question: A Moore machine is in state q1, whose associated output is 1. It reads input 0 and stays in q1, then reads input 1 and stays in q1. What output is associated with q1 after each of these inputs?

options.B: No output, since q1 is not final

questions.explanation: In a Moore machine the output depends solely on the present state, so staying in q1 always gives output 1 regardless of the input read.

questions.question: C++ was designed by ____ at ____.
questions.explanation: Bjarne Stroustrup created C++ at Bell Laboratories. Dennis Ritchie created C and James Gosling created Java.

questions.question: How is an IPv6 address written?

options.A: Six pairs of hexadecimal digits separated by hyphens
options.B: Four decimal numbers separated by periods
options.C: Eight groups of hexadecimal numbers separated by colons
options.D: Eight groups of decimal numbers separated by periods

questions.explanation: IPv6 is 128 bits written as eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons; four dotted decimals is IPv4.

questions.concept: Match the Sum game termination condition
questions.question: In the 'Match the Sum' game with 15 cells, new digits keep entering at the rightmost end while existing digits shift left. When does the game end?

options.B: When there is no empty cell left to insert a digit
options.C: When the student types a wrong sum
options.D: When the digit 9 appears in every cell

questions.explanation: The game continues until there is no empty cell to insert a new digit.

questions.question: What is the main aim of the Web of Things (WoT)?

options.A: To limit IoT devices to wired LANs only
options.B: To replace sensors with web browsers
options.C: To provide one interface to connect many devices
options.D: To give every device its own separate app

questions.explanation: WoT uses web services to connect physical-world things and aims to provide one interface for many devices rather than a separate app for each.

questions.question: In two-tier DBMS architecture, clients connect using ODBC. What does ODBC stand for?
questions.explanation: ODBC stands for Open Database Connectivity; JDBC is Java Database Connectivity.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an actuator in IoT?
questions.explanation: Stepper motors, fans and LEDs produce physical output and act as actuators; Arduino is a microcontroller platform, not an actuator.

questions.question: Which of the following are basic refresh modes for dynamic RAM? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The two basic DRAM refresh modes are burst refresh and distributed refresh.

questions.question: A deque can behave like a stack when:

options.A: insertion is done at the rear and deletion at the front
options.B: insertion is done at both ends and deletion at none
options.C: deletion is done alternately from front and rear
options.D: insertion and deletion are both done at the same end

questions.explanation: Inserting and deleting at the same end gives LIFO (stack) behaviour; rear insertion with front deletion gives queue (FIFO) behaviour.
